title: Mandatory Gear, CHIANG DAO 160 and ELEPHANT 100 — Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB
publisher: UTMB World Series / HOKA Chiang Mai Thailand by UTMB
claims: CHIANG DAO 160 and ELEPHANT 100 share one mandatory equipment table, separate from the PAGODA 50, HMONG 50, SUTHEP 20 and CHEDI 20 tables.

The shared mandatory list contains 14 items: running pack, mobile phone, personal collapsible cup of at least 150 ml, at least 1 litre of water, one working headlamp with spare cells, survival blanket of at least 1.40 m x 2 m, food, waterproof jacket with hood and DWR protection, LED/flashing light or reflective vest/belt, first-aid kit, whistle, cap/bandana/buff, reusable bowl with spoon or spork, and passport or ID card.
The mandatory shell for these two races is a waterproof jacket with hood and DWR protection, whereas the PAGODA 50 table lists a windproof jacket.
Bottles or flasks with lids are not accepted in place of the collapsible cup, and water may not be carried in plastic bags or ziplock bags.
The mandatory water minimum is 1 litre, and food is listed with a recommendation of 800 kcal rather than a fixed requirement.
The mandatory first-aid kit should include wound care and pain relievers, with NSAIDs prohibited.
The phone must stay on for the whole race with airplane mode forbidden, an external battery is highly recommended, and a LiveTrail or LiveRun application is required.

The recommended gear list for these two races adds trekking poles, a GPS watch, sunglasses, arm sleeves, warm gloves, spare warm clothing, long trousers or socks, Vaseline or anti-heat cream and THB 500 in cash.
The page states that the organiser may add items to the mandatory list according to the weather forecast, with the final list confirmed one or two days before the race.
